text:
Samir Patel: Quick qheading to the Inference Summit from SFO, got a 10h layover in Reykjavk before the connection. Anyone survived a long layover + red-eye combo? Tips for staying sane?
Dana Ortiz: Oh hah, yes. Long layovers can be a blessing if you plan. Book a day room near the airport if you can, otherwise scout an airport lounge (pay-per-use options exist).
Tom Becker: If you're stuck in the terminal: find a quieter gate area, away from family zones. Buy a cheap neck pillow and earplugs if you don't have them. Noise-cancelling buds = miracle.
Priya Nair: Pro tip: refresh your phone/eSIM before you land so you can book things quickly. Download offline maps for the transfer city, and put all boarding passes in Apple Wallet/GPay.
sasha-bot: Reminder: add flight + layover details to the team itinerary spreadsheet so we can time airport pickups.
Samir Patel: Any rules about leaving transit area to explore the city during a long layover? My transit time is 10h incl. customs.
Dana Ortiz: Depends on the country and visa. For Reykjavk (Iceland) you clear passport control, so you can step out. Check minimum connection time—but 10h is usually fine. Leave at least 2.5-3h back to re-clear security.
Tom Becker: Also factor luggage: if it's checked through to the final destination you can leave without baggage hassle. If not, use a left-luggage service at the airport so you can wander unencumbered.
Priya Nair: Currency: grab a couple of local bills at the airport ATM, but your card will likely work almost everywhere. For tiny purchases or taxis, cash helps.
Samir Patel: What's the smartest way to sleep on a 6h stretch in the airport vs. on the plane?
Dana Ortiz: Short naps in the terminal, full sleep on the plane if you can recline. Try to align a long sleep with the second leg of the journey so you land refreshed.
Tom Becker: If you plan to sleep in the terminal: pick a quiet corner, keep valuables zipped and phone in airplane mode but alarm set. Consider a charger nearby; battery banks are clutch.
Priya Nair: For carry-on-only: Pack an outfit swap in a compression bag. If you get stuck, you have a clean set. Also bring a small microfibre towel for cold showers in lounges.
Samir Patel: Anything conference-specific (e.g., plugging in + hot spot for demos)?
Dana Ortiz: Bring a compact multi-port USB-C charger and a short HDMI or display dongle if you demo. Conference rooms rarely have enough power outlets. Also pack a small ethernet adapter if you need stable demo networking.
Priya Nair: Save a zipped folder of your demo repo + credentials (encrypted). If you need to hotfix in an airport lounge, you don't want to download 2GB of deps.
Tom Becker: If you have time between flights, look up nearby green spaces/quick tours. Even 2 hours outside gives you sunlight and helps reset your clock.
Samir Patel: Can someone throw together a tiny "layover survival kit" checklist I can screenshot?
Dana Ortiz: Surehere's my minimalist kit (fits in a laptop backpack):
```
- passport + printed and digital boarding passes
- phone + USB-C cable + multi-port charger
- 20-30k mAh power bank
- travel adapter (check country plug)
- neck pillow + eye mask + foam earplugs
- 1 clean change of clothes in compression bag
- small toiletries (toothpaste/tablets, deodorant stick)
- quick-dry towel + wipes
- 2 protein bars + electrolyte sachets
- travel insurance card + emergency contacts
- small cash in local currency + credit card
- zip bag for liquids (100ml)
- eSIM or local SIM info preloaded
- laptop with critical files zipped + password manager access
```
Samir Patel: Awesome, saving that. Anyone have lounge recs in KEF (Reykjavik)?
Dana Ortiz: I used the Plaza Premium at KEF last yearquiet, showers, decent food. Worth the fee for a long layover.
Tom Becker: If you're feeling cheeky, try to time a nap + shower then go for a 45-60 minute quick city circuit. Reykjavk airport is close to the city center.
Priya Nair: Final note: reset your watch/phone to destination timezone asap and get sunlight exposure when possible. It'll cut jetlag by a day.
Samir Patel: You guys are amazing. I'll grab a lounge pass and pack the kit. Will update the itinerary. Thanks! :raised_hands:
